rationale: Roadmap exhausted: 5 of 7 remaining SPEC items (chunk 1b DuckDB persistence, decision log, markout instrumentation, calibration reporting, fee-coverage) are fully scoped and brief-consistent but blocked_by_policy because automation.allow has no dependencies entry; the 6th (live fee-schedule refresh) needs a manual PDF-sourcing decision. after.question: Allow-list the `dependencies` change class in automation.allow for ai-engineering-markets (currently empty under mode: build)? This unblocks 5 of 7 remaining SPEC items: chunk 1b (DuckDB persistence), the decision log, markout instrumentation, and calibration reporting (all chained on one pinned duckdb version), plus the fee-coverage field (one pinned PDF-extraction library) — all already satisfy the brief's own 'stdlib-plus-DuckDB bias: pin every new dependency in a manifest' constraint, so this is activating already-planned work, not expanding scope. Without it, no further item in docs/SPEC.md can ever validate ready. Chunk 2b (LLM-backed classification) would still additionally need network.allowed:true and an API key, so allow-listing dependencies alone does not open that item.

How should the current (post-Feb-2026) Kalshi fee-schedule PDF be sourced? The live PDF has 429-blocked automated fetch twice with no Wayback capture since Feb 2026, and this contract sets network.allowed:false so no command available to the builder can fetch it. Options include a manual residential-browser download filed under research/data/ with a capture-date filename, or explicitly accepting the Feb 2026 snapshot as the interim fee_coverage source and deferring refresh.
